questions.question: What is a residual for an observed data point?
What does a positive residual mean?
choices: The observed point lies above the fitted line
The point lies below the fitted line
The x-value is above its mean

questions.question: What does a negative residual mean?
choices: The point lies above the fitted line
The observed point lies below the fitted line

questions.question: An observed y-value is 12 and its prediction is 10. What is the residual?
An observed y-value is 7 and its prediction is 11. What is the residual?
What does a zero residual mean?
choices: The prediction equals the observed value for that point
The entire data set has no variation

questions.question: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a residual plot?
choices: The original units squared in every case

questions.question: Why is a curved pattern in a residual plot a concern for a linear model?
choices: It proves all observations are wrong
It suggests systematic nonlinear structure remains

questions.question: What residual pattern generally supports a linear model?
For ŷ = 2x + 1 and point (3, 9), what is the residual?
Why do least-squares calculations square residuals?
choices: To make each residual equal to its prediction
To force the line through the origin
To penalize deviations without sign cancellation

questions.question: What does a large absolute residual identify?
choices: A point with a necessarily large x-value
A point poorly predicted by the model
A point that must be removed

questions.question: If residual spread grows as x increases, what does that suggest?
choices: Prediction variability may increase with x
The model explains every outcome exactly

questions.question: Why does a small residual at one point not prove a model is good overall?
choices: Fit must be assessed across the data and context
One point always determines the best line
A residual can never equal zero
All models with intercepts are inaccurate

questions.question: In ordinary least-squares regression with an intercept, what is the sum of the fitted residuals, apart from numerical rounding?
Model A has residuals 1, −1, 2. Model B has 2, −2, 1 on the same data. Which has smaller sum of squared residuals?
For ŷ = 20 − 2x, an observed point is (4, 9). What is the residual?
A residual is −5. How should the prediction be described for that point?
choices: It overestimates the observed value by 5
It underestimates the observed value by 5

questions.question: A residual plot has no obvious curve but contains one extreme residual. What is a reasonable next step?
choices: Remove it without checking the observation
Judge fit using only that single residual
Ignore it because the plot has no curve
Investigate the point and its influence
